nodes.description: Public mapping (address => uint256) recording the ETH deposited by each account
Public bool flag tracking whether the contract has already bought the tokens
Public uint256 recording the ETH value of tokens currently held by the contract
Public uint256 maximum amount of user ETH the contract will accept (500 ether, raised to 1000 ether)
Public constant uint256 minimum ETH (60 ether) that must be deposited before the buy-in
Public address of the contract owner, set to the deployer
Public address of the crowdsale/presale wallet that receives the ETH
Constructor that sets owner = msg.sender
Lets a depositor withdraw a proportional share of tokens after the buy-in using a caller-supplied ERC20 address
Lets any caller withdraw their recorded ETH balance before the buy-in
Owner-only buy-in that forwards contract ETH to the sale address and records contract_eth_value
Owner-only function that raises eth_cap to 1000 ether
Payable default function that records incoming user ETH deposits in balances
msg.sender used in the constructor to assign the owner
msg.sender used as caller and token recipient in perform_withdrawal
msg.sender used as caller and ETH recipient in refund_me
msg.sender compared against owner to authorize buy_the_tokens
msg.sender compared against owner to authorize upgrade_cap
msg.sender used as depositor key in the payable fallback
External call token.balanceOf(address(this)) on a user-supplied token address, which can execute attacker code
External ERC20 token.transfer(msg.sender, tokens_to_withdraw) on a user-supplied token address
Unchecked subtraction contract_eth_value -= balances[msg.sender], which can underflow
Low-level ETH send msg.sender.transfer(eth_to_withdraw) that executes untrusted code at the recipient
Unchecked low-level call sale.call.value(contract_eth_value)() forwarding all contract ETH
Unchecked addition balances[msg.sender] += msg.value, which can overflow
User-supplied ERC20 token address argument of perform_withdrawal
ERC20 instance created by casting tokenAddress inside perform_withdrawal
Local holding the result of token.balanceOf(address(this))
Local proportional token amount computed from balances[msg.sender], token balance and contract_eth_value
Local holding balances[msg.sender] before it is zeroed in refund_me

edges.reason: msg.sender triggers the constructor execution
owner state variable is assigned directly from msg.sender
constructor writes the owner state variable
msg.sender invokes perform_withdrawal
require(bought_tokens) gates the withdrawal
tokenAddress parameter is cast into the ERC20 token instance
token instance is used to perform the balanceOf external call
balanceOf return value is stored in contract_token_balance
token balance is used to compute tokens_to_withdraw
balances[msg.sender] is used to compute tokens_to_withdraw
contract_eth_value is used as the divisor of the token share computation
tokens_to_withdraw is passed to token.transfer
token instance is used to perform the transfer external call
balances[msg.sender] is subtracted from contract_eth_value; underflows if it exceeds contract_eth_value
contract_eth_value is decremented without an underflow guard
attacker-controlled token.transfer can reenter perform_withdrawal
transfer executes code at the msg.sender address
balances[msg.sender] is set to zero before the external transfer
msg.sender invokes refund_me
eth_to_withdraw is loaded from balances[msg.sender]
eth_to_withdraw is sent to msg.sender
ETH send executes untrusted code at the msg.sender address
untrusted recipient fallback can reenter refund_me
balances[msg.sender] is zeroed before the ETH send
require(msg.sender == owner) authorizes buy_the_tokens
owner is compared with msg.sender to guard the buy-in
require(!bought_tokens) short-circuits repeated buys
require(sale != 0x0) validates the destination address
require(this.balance >= min_required_amount) gates the buy-in
buy_the_tokens sets bought_tokens to true
buy_the_tokens records contract_eth_value = this.balance
contract_eth_value is the ETH value forwarded to the sale address
buy_the_tokens invokes the low-level sale call
unchecked sale.call can reenter buy_the_tokens
require(msg.sender == owner) authorizes upgrade_cap
owner is compared with msg.sender to guard the cap upgrade
upgrade_cap overwrites eth_cap with 1000 ether
msg.sender sends ETH to the payable fallback
require(!bought_tokens) blocks deposits after the buy-in
require(this.balance + msg.value < eth_cap) enforces the deposit cap
fallback performs the balance addition operation
balances[msg.sender] += msg.value can overflow the recorded balance
msg.sender is used as the mapping index of the overflow-prone arithmetic

normalization_plan.reason: The tokenAddress parameter exists only inside perform_withdrawal and should be folded into that function node
The ERC20 token instance is a short-lived local created by casting tokenAddress inside perform_withdrawal
The local only stores the return value of the token.balanceOf external call and should be merged into that unsafe operation
The local is computed solely to be passed to token.transfer and should be merged into that unsafe operation
The local only holds balances[msg.sender] before it is sent via msg.sender.transfer and should be merged into that unsafe operation
